title: Understanding the Nature of Foreign Trade

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why countries like Nigeria import goods from other nations? Foreign trade is crucial for economic growth and development.

blocks.markdown: Foreign trade refers to the exchange of goods and services between countries. It includes three main types: **import**, **export**, and **entrepôt trade**. **Imports** are goods brought into a country, **exports** are goods sent out, and **entrepôt trade** involves the import of goods for export without significant transformation.

blocks.title: Definition of Foreign Trade
blocks.text: Foreign trade is the exchange of goods and services across international borders, allowing countries to obtain resources they lack.

blocks.markdown: Countries engage in foreign trade for various reasons, such as acquiring goods not available domestically, accessing cheaper products, and enhancing international relations. Trade can be classified into **visible trade**, which involves tangible goods, and **invisible trade**, which includes services such as tourism and banking.

The **balance of trade** is the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports, while the **balance of payments** includes all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

blocks.title: Calculating Balance of Trade
blocks.prompt: If Nigeria exports goods worth ₦500 million and imports goods worth ₦300 million, what is the balance of trade?

steps.text: Identify the values of exports and imports.
Subtract the total imports from total exports: ₦500 million - ₦300 million.

blocks.answer: The balance of trade is ₦200 million.

blocks.markdown: Foreign trade has its advantages and disadvantages. Advantages include access to a wider variety of goods, potential for economic growth, and job creation. Disadvantages may involve dependency on foreign goods, trade imbalances, and exposure to global economic fluctuations.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When answering questions about foreign trade, clearly distinguish between imports, exports, and entrepôt trade to avoid losing marks.

points: Foreign trade is essential for countries to access goods and services they cannot produce domestically.
Visible trade involves tangible goods, while invisible trade includes services.
Understanding the balance of trade and payments is crucial for evaluating a country's economic health.
